pre_registered_claim.C: ACL force/strain during a sidestep cut scales with the COMBINED knee-abduction(valgus) + anterior-shear + internal-tibial-rotation load (multiplanar); a sagittal-plane-only (anterior-shear-alone) model FAILS to reach ACL-injury force; hamstring co-contraction REDUCES anterior shear (protective).
pre_registered_claim.not_C: Sagittal-plane loading alone (anterior drawer / quadriceps-dominant shear) is sufficient to explain ACL injury force; frontal-plane (valgus) and transverse-plane (internal rotation) loads are incidental, not causally additive; hamstring co-contraction has no protective effect on ACL loading.
pre_registered_claim.threshold_preregistered: Sagittal-alone falsifier: peak anterior drawer force must NOT exceed the 2000N ACL-failure-force criterion under realistic perturbation (McLean 2004's own pre-set criterion, not fit post hoc). Hamstring falsifier: >=2 independent cadaveric/in-situ studies must show >=15% ACL-force or anterior-translation reduction under physiological co-contraction, p<0.05.
pre_registered_claim.adversary_forced: valgus/frontal-plane loading is harmless in isolation OR baseline single-timepoint KAM screening reliably predicts which specific athlete will tear their ACL (the strongest fair form of the 'valgus doesn't matter' adversary is the population-level prospective-classifier claim, not the mechanistic one — forced via the Cronstrom 2020 9-cohort pooled meta-analysis, the largest available fair test).

falsifier_tests.measure: cadaveric ACL force under dual-combination loading states

evidence.cite: Markolf KL, Burchfield DM, Shapiro MM, Shepard MF, Finerman GA, Slauterbeck JL. Combined knee loading states that generate high anterior cruciate ligament forces. J Orthop Res. 1995;13(6):930-5.
evidence.n: in-vitro cadaveric knees (dual-load combinations swept 90deg flex -> 5deg hyperextension)
evidence.value: Applied loads: 100N anterior tibial force (ATF), 10Nm varus/valgus, 10Nm internal/external tibial torque. ATF+internal tibial torque combo produced the HIGHEST ACL force recorded in the whole study, concentrated at full extension/hyperextension. ATF+valgus moment increased force at FLEXED positions. ATF+external torque DECREASED force (near-total unloading by ~90deg flexion).

evidence.cite: Navacchia A, Bates NA, Schilaty ND, Krych AJ, Hewett TE. Knee Abduction and Internal Rotation Moments Increase ACL Force During Landing Through the Posterior Slope of the Tibia. J Orthop Res. 2019;37(8):1730-1742.
evidence.n: 4 subject-specific FE knee models (2M/2F), validated vs cadaveric impact-rig kinematics+strain
evidence.value: Model validation: kinematics RMSE<1.5mm/2deg, r>0.75; ACL strain RMSE<2%, r>0.9. Model-predicted ACL force vs anterior component of lateral-plateau tibiofemoral contact force: r=0.99. Larger KAM + larger internal tibial rotation torque (ITR) BOTH increase this anterior contact-force component via the posterior tibial slope.

falsifier_tests.note: Two methodologically decorrelated approaches 24 years apart (direct dial-in cadaveric mechanical testing, 1995; validated finite-element model matched to an independent cadaveric impact-rig, 2019) converge: valgus and internal rotation do not load a separate structure — they geometrically couple onto the SAME ACL fiber tension via the tibial plateau's posterior slope + the ACL's own oblique fiber axis (see mechanism.geometric_derivation).

falsifier_tests.verdict: PASS (this is the decisive falsifier the task pre-registered)
falsifier_tests.measure: forward-dynamics musculoskeletal model, stochastic perturbation, sidestep cutting

evidence.cite: McLean SG, Huang X, Su A, van den Bogert AJ. Sagittal plane biomechanics cannot injure the ACL during sidestep cutting. Clin Biomech. 2004;19(8):828-38.
evidence.n: 20 subject-specific models (10M/10F), n=5000 random perturbations of initial contact + muscle activation
evidence.value: Injury criterion (pre-set, not fit post hoc): anterior drawer force > 2000N. RESULT: peak anterior drawer force NEVER exceeded 2000N in ANY of the 5000 perturbed simulations. Valgus loads DID reach injury-capable magnitudes, more frequently in female models than male.

falsifier_tests.note: A clean, quantitative, pre-registered-threshold falsifier: the sagittal-only mechanism was FORCED to its strongest fair form (5000 stochastic perturbations of a realistic subject-specific model, not a single nominal trial) and it FAILED to reach the injury criterion in 100% of trials, while the multiplanar (valgus) route succeeded — exactly the asymmetric result the task's falsifier demanded.

falsifier_tests.measure: cadaveric robotic universal-force-moment-sensor (UFS), in-situ ACL force under quadriceps vs quadriceps+hamstring loading

evidence.cite: Li G, Rudy TW, Sakane M, Kanamori A, Ma CB, Woo SL. The importance of quadriceps and hamstring muscle loading on knee kinematics and in-situ forces in the ACL. J Biomech. 1999;32(4):395-400.
evidence.value: 200N quadriceps load alone: ACL in-situ force rises from 27.8+/-9.3N (full ext) to 44.9+/-13.8N peak at 15deg flexion. Adding 80N antagonistic hamstring load reduces ACL in-situ force by 30% (15deg), 43% (30deg), 44% (60deg) (all p<0.05), and reduces anterior tibial translation 18%, lateral translation 46%, internal tibial rotation 30% at 30deg (p<0.05).

falsifier_tests.note: Direct, quantitative, statistically-significant confirmation of the protective mechanism at the exact ACL in-situ force level (not just kinematics) — satisfies the pre-registered >=15%/p<0.05 threshold with a wide margin (30-44% reduction).

geometric_mechanism.derivation: The ACL is a single oblique fiber bundle (femoral posterolateral condyle -> tibial anteromedial plateau), not three independent structures for three planes. Two geometric coupling paths force multiplanar loads onto the SAME ligament tension, which a sagittal-only free-body model sets to zero by construction: (1) TIBIAL POSTERIOR SLOPE: the lateral tibial plateau slopes posteriorly-downward; an applied knee-abduction (valgus) moment increases lateral-compartment compressive contact force, which the posterior slope's geometry converts into an ADDITIONAL anterior-directed shear component on the lateral tibial plateau (Navacchia 2019's directly-modeled mechanism, r=0.99 to ACL force) -- this SUMS with the sagittal-plane anterior shear already present from GRF/quadriceps pull, on the same ligament. (2) OBLIQUE-FIBER WIND-UP: internal tibial rotation twists the tibia under the femoral condyles along the ACL's own long axis, tightening (winding) its oblique fibers independent of flexion angle -- the same geometric fact that makes the clinical pivot-shift test (valgus+IR+flexion-extension combined) more sensitive for ACL deficiency than the anterior-drawer test (sagittal alone). A sagittal-only model zeroes both coupling terms, which is exactly why McLean 2004's sagittal-alone simulation structurally cannot reach the 2000N criterion (F3) while the combined-load Markolf/Navacchia mechanism can (F2).
geometric_mechanism.consequence: This is why 'a sagittal-plane-only model must fail' is not a statistical accident of one dataset -- it is a structural prediction of the joint's own articular geometry, independently confirmed by 2 decorrelated methods (F2) and directly falsified/confirmed by a 3rd (F3).

anchor_1.cite: Hewett TE, Myer GD, Ford KR, Heidt RS Jr, Colosimo AJ, McLean SG, van den Bogert AJ, Paterno MV, Succop P. Biomechanical measures of neuromuscular control and valgus loading of the knee predict anterior cruciate ligament injury risk in female athletes: a prospective study. Am J Sports Med. 2005;33(4):492-501.
anchor_1.measured_this_study: Knee abduction angle at landing 8deg greater in injured (p<.05). Injured athletes had a 2.5x GREATER knee abduction moment (p<.001) and 20% higher GRF (p<.05); stance time 16% SHORTER. KAM predicted ACL-injury status at 73% specificity / 78% sensitivity. Dynamic valgus composite measure: predictive r^2=0.88.
anchor_1.headline_precision_correction: The commonly-quoted '4-6 fold' figure is this paper's BACKGROUND citation of the pre-existing, separately-established female:male ACL injury INCIDENCE RATE ratio (stated in its own Introduction as prior literature), NOT this study's own new KAM-risk-ratio finding, which is the 2.5x group-difference in KAM above. Conflating the two overstates precision; both are real but answer different questions (population sex-disparity in incidence vs within-female-cohort KAM group difference).
anchor_1.unverified_in_this_pass: The frequently-cited '25.25 Nm' KAM cutoff value does not appear in the abstract text fetched live this session -- it is a full-text/Table figure. Not independently re-derived from primary full text here; flagged per this repo's own established citation-precision convention (do not silently propagate a secondary-source number as if abstract-verified).

anchor_2_decorrelated_instrument.cite: Zazulak BT, Hewett TE, Reeves NP, Goldberg B, Cholewicki J. Deficits in neuromuscular control of the trunk predict knee injury risk: a prospective biomechanical-epidemiologic study. Am J Sports Med. 2007;35(7):1123-30.
anchor_2_decorrelated_instrument.measured_this_study: Trunk displacement after sudden force release (a CORE/postural perturbation test, not a jump-landing knee kinematics/kinetics measurement) was greater in athletes with knee/ligament/ACL injury (p<.05). LATERAL (coronal), not sagittal, displacement was the STRONGEST predictor of ligament injury (p=.009). Logistic model (trunk displacement + proprioception + LBP history) predicted knee ligament injury: 91% sensitivity / 68% specificity; predicted ACL injury in FEMALES with 91% accuracy (not significant in males).
anchor_2_decorrelated_instrument.common_mode_flag: Shares senior author (Hewett TE) with anchor_1 -- a genuinely DIFFERENT measurement instrument and hidden state (whole-body postural/core control vs knee-specific 3D kinematics/kinetics) from a DIFFERENT subject cohort (277 mixed-sex collegiate athletes vs 205 female-only), so this is a real decorrelation on instrument+cohort, but NOT on research-program/lab -- reported honestly, not oversold as fully independent.

adversary_forced_meta_analysis.cite: Cronstrom A, Creaby MW, Ageberg E. Do knee abduction kinematics and kinetics predict future anterior cruciate ligament injury risk? A systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies. BMC Musculoskelet Disord. 2020;21(1):563.
adversary_forced_meta_analysis.measured: Pooled across 9 prospective studies: NEITHER 3D KAM angle at initial contact (mean diff -1.68, 95%CI -4.49 to 1.14, n_injured=66/n_ctrl=1369), peak 3D abduction angle (mean diff -2.17, CI -7.22 to 2.89, n=25/563), 2D peak abduction angle (mean diff -3.25, CI -9.86 to 3.36, n=8/302), 2D medial displacement (mean diff -0.19cm, CI -0.96 to 0.38, n=72/967), NOR peak knee abduction MOMENT (mean diff -10.61, 95%CI -26.73 to 5.50, n_injured=54/n_ctrl=1330) significantly predicted future ACL injury. Point estimates trend in the OPPOSITE direction from anchor_1's within-study finding (injured slightly LOWER, not higher, though CI wide and crosses zero).
adversary_forced_meta_analysis.verdict: This is the adversary FORCED to its strongest fair form (largest available pooled N, PRISMA systematic review, 9 independent cohorts) for the EPIDEMIOLOGICAL claim specifically. It survives: baseline single-timepoint KAM measured in healthy athletes does NOT reliably classify which individual will tear their ACL years later, at the current evidence base.
adversary_forced_meta_analysis.resolution_symmetric_QC: The mechanistic claim (F1-F4: combined multiplanar loading generates higher ACL force than sagittal alone, in a cut, and hamstrings protect against it) is a physics/cadaver-mechanics claim, robust to population sampling noise, and stands PASS. The prospective-INJURY-CLASSIFIER claim (a single baseline KAM value predicts which specific athlete gets hurt) is a much harder population-inference claim and is NOT supported once fairly pooled -- these are DIFFERENT claims and must not be conflated. This mirrors this same repo's own prior finding (MSK-CUTTING-ACL-LOAD's 'anticipated>unanticipated' anchor was similarly refuted on a single study; here the refutation is even stronger, a 9-study meta-analysis, not one paper).

sex_difference.cite: Ford KR, Myer GD, Hewett TE. Valgus knee motion during landing in high school female and male basketball players. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2003;35(10):1745-50.
sex_difference.measured: Female athletes (n=47) landed with significantly greater total valgus knee motion and greater max valgus angle than males (n=34) during a drop vertical jump; females also showed significant side-to-side (limb dominance) asymmetry in max valgus angle.

fatigue.cite: McLean SG, Fellin RE, Suedekum N, Calabrese G, Passerallo A, Joy S. Impact of fatigue on gender-based high-risk landing strategies. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2007;39(3):502-14.
fatigue.measured: Fatigue increased initial-contact and peak-stance knee abduction and internal rotation motions, and peak knee internal-rotation/adduction/abduction MOMENTS -- the abduction-moment fatigue effect was more pronounced in females (3-way ANOVA, Bonferroni alpha=0.002).

besier_2001.cite: Besier TF, Lloyd DG, Ackland TR, Cochrane JL. Anticipatory effects on knee joint loading during running and cutting maneuvers. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2001;33(7):1176-81.
besier_2001.measured: Unanticipated (UN) cutting: varus/valgus and internal/external rotation moments up to 2x the preplanned (PP) condition magnitude; sagittal flexion/extension moments SIMILAR between PP and UN.

giesche_2021_meta_analysis.cite: Giesche F, Stief F, Groneberg DA, Wilke J. Effect of unplanned athletic movement on knee mechanics: a systematic review with multilevel meta-analysis. Br J Sports Med. 2021;55(23):1366-1378.
giesche_2021_meta_analysis.measured: Unplanned tasks -> significantly higher external knee ABDUCTION moment (SMD 0.34, 95%CI 0.16-0.51, 14 studies) AND tibial INTERNAL ROTATION moment (SMD 0.51, 95%CI 0.23-0.79, 11 studies). NO significant difference for SAGITTAL-plane mechanics. Effect larger in non-professional athletes (SMD 0.55).

mai_2022_nuance.cite: Mai P et al. (see F1 above, PMID 36439622)
mai_2022_nuance.measured: WITHIN complexity-matched tasks, true unanticipation (task3, 1.64 Nm/kg) did not exceed a complex-but-preplanned task (task2, 1.73 Nm/kg) -- a genuine, disclosed minority finding at n=51 against Giesche's larger pooled direction; both clearly exceed the simplest preplanned task (task1, 1.52 Nm/kg).

kristianslund_2013_scope_boundary.measured: Poor cross-task rank correlation for KAM specifically between drop-jump and sidestep-cut (rho=0.135) despite moderate correlation for valgus ANGLE (rho=0.706) -- a drop-vertical-jump screening test (Hewett 2005's own task) does not reliably rank-order athletes' actual cutting-task KAM.

task_specificity_and_reactive_cutting.synthesis: Reactive/unanticipated demand robustly (pooled, 25 trials) elevates FRONTAL+TRANSVERSE plane knee loading specifically, leaving sagittal loading unchanged -- consistent with, and mechanistically coherent with, F2/F3's finding that the dangerous load is multiplanar, not sagittal. This directly instantiates the task's 'position of no return' framing: a reactive, late-decision cut is measurably (not just anecdotally) loaded differently, and specifically more dangerously, than a rehearsed one.

Gross valgus ANGLE (not moment) may be a coarser, lower-precision flag (Turner 2024 CMC 0.47-0.78 is degraded but non-zero — a large, qualitative deviation e.g. >15-20deg might still be flaggable even if a precise Nm value is not), but this was not directly tested by the sources above and should not be assumed.
